metadata.title: What Does Claude Actually Do When You Say "Clean This Data"?
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude decides, using its own judgment, what looks messy in a spreadsheet and fixes it -- or is doing something narrower. Lands the carry-out that cleaning a sheet is one fixed checklist run in order, and a column that comes back clean has been reformatted, not fact-checked.

beats.narration_text: Someone asks whether cleaning messy spreadsheet data means Claude uses its own judgment. It doesn't. Liam is here to take you through exactly what the skill does, step by step.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'What decides what gets cleaned -- judgment?', hesitates on 'judgment', corrects to 'a checklist', lands the real question

props.text:
What decides
what gets cleaned —

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('judgment' -> 'a checklist') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: The natural guess is that "clean this data" means Claude decides, using its own judgment, what looks wrong and fixes it. But the skill runs one fixed checklist: trim whitespace, fix inconsistent casing, convert numbers stored as text, standardize dates, remove duplicates, and flag mixed-type columns -- nothing more. Give it a column where the same currency symbol covers two different currencies, no way to tell them apart. That's not on the checklist. No step resolves currency confusion, so the column comes out exactly as ambiguous as it went in.

shot.new_visual_element: A judgment figure weighing what 'looks messy', struck through; a fixed six-step checklist lit instead

production_viz.label: Judgment, struck -- checklist, lit
production_viz.mechanic: Left: a figure icon labelled 'JUDGMENT' beside a thought-bubble of scattered decision marks. Right: a card labelled 'THE CHECKLIST -- SIX STEPS' listing three grouped lines. The judgment side dims and gets a terracotta strike; the checklist side stays lit. A final line reads 'two currencies, one symbol -- not on the list' and the checklist does not reach for it.

beats.narration_text: What the skill actually does: it runs six fixed steps, in order -- trim, fix casing, convert numbers, standardize dates, dedupe, flag mixed types -- nothing beyond that list. Watch the anchor: one Revenue column holding " 1,200 ", "1300", "N/A", and " 1,400.00 ". Whitespace gets trimmed. The number-like text converts to real numbers. "N/A" can't convert, so the column gets flagged mixed-type instead. Then it stops, waiting.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR -- one Revenue column traveling RAW -> TRIMMED -> CONVERTED -> FLAGGED, then stopping

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR -- one column, four stops
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Four stacked cards labelled 'RAW', 'TRIMMED', 'CONVERTED', 'FLAGGED'. A single highlighted token 'REVENUE COLUMN' travels down through all four cards in turn, each lighting as it arrives. At the bottom, the token halts beside a label 'N/A -- flagged, waiting' -- it does not continue past the flagged card. THIS EXACT COMPOSITION RETURNS, PAID OFF, AT B03.

beats.narration_text: The Revenue column comes back trimmed, converted, and flagged -- "N/A" still sitting there, marked for a human to look at. But converting "1,200" to a number doesn't mean it's the right number: a typo that should read "12,000" converts just as cleanly. And a flagged mixed-type column isn't automatically broken -- an ID column that mixes numbers and letters on purpose gets the same flag. Either way, the cleaned sheet still waits for someone to check what the checklist can't: whether the values themselves are correct.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS, trimmed/converted/flagged; splits into 'converted cleanly is not correct' and 'flagged is not broken'

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- flagged, then split
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 FOUR-CARD COMPOSITION RETURNS, identical placement, the token resting at the 'FLAGGED' card beside 'N/A -- flagged, waiting'. It shrinks and slides up. Two cards fade in beneath: left reads 'CONVERTED: 1,200' with a checkmark, then a struck-through 'CORRECT?' beneath it, labelled 'converted cleanly is not correct'; right reads 'FLAGGED: MIXED-TYPE' beside a faint 'on purpose, maybe' note, labelled 'flagged is not broken'.

beats.narration_text: Clean this data doesn't mean Claude judges what looks messy and fixes it -- it runs one fixed checklist, in order, and anything outside that list is untouched. A column that comes back clean has been reformatted, not fact-checked.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt -- read it with me. Give Claude a spreadsheet with a messy column -- mixed date formats, extra whitespace, a duplicate row or two -- and ask it to run the clean-data-xls skill. Then add one problem that's not on its checklist, like the same currency symbol covering two different currencies, and run it again. Watch what changes, and what doesn't. Liam, in for Bear.
